subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the inverse of the matrix A with rows (1, 2) and (3, −5).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.86 — VSAQ chapter 15 Matrices, answer 111.2. Printed appearances: AP 18 · TS 22. ⚠ THE 1+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. recall_prompt: Say how you would find the inverse of this two by two matrix.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find |A| and Adj A
steps.margin_note: First mark. |A| is negative here, which is fine — it only has to be non-zero. Then use the 2×2 shortcut for the adjoint.

recall.must_convey: That |A| is found (−11, non-zero) and that the 2×2 adjoint swaps the diagonal and flips the sign of the other two entries.
accept: the determinant is minus eleven and the adjoint swaps the diagonal and changes the other signs
find the determinant then use the two by two adjoint shortcut
determinant minus eleven which is not zero so the inverse exists
determinant minus eleven, adjoint ki diagonal swap chesi signs marchali
swap the diagonal entries and negate the off diagonal ones

steps.why: A negative determinant is perfectly normal. The only thing that matters is that it is not zero, because that is what would make the inverse impossible.
common_mistakes: Taking |A| as 5 − 6 and forgetting the sign of the first product.
Refusing to continue because the determinant is negative.

steps.label: Divide by |A|
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Dividing by −11 flips every sign as well as scaling — so the three negative entries become positive and the positive one becomes negative.

recall.must_convey: That A⁻¹ is the adjoint divided by −11, and that dividing by a negative flips every sign.
accept: divide the adjoint by minus eleven so every sign flips giving five elevenths and two elevenths on top
A inverse is one over minus eleven times the adjoint
dividing by the negative determinant changes all the signs
minus eleven tho divide cheste anni signs marutai
the inverse is five by eleven, two by eleven, three by eleven and minus one by eleven

steps.why: Dividing by a negative number changes the sign of every entry. Missing that turns all four signs of the answer upside down.
common_mistakes: Writing the inverse with the adjoint signs unchanged.
